title: Agentic media runtime reframes publishing as governed interpretation

signal.summary: Media systems can use AI not just to generate articles, but to classify signals, enforce policy, structure interpretation, and prepare approved distribution drafts.
signal.why_now: The rise of AI agents makes it necessary to separate interpretation, transformation, approval, publishing, and memory updates.

context: JAZEKKER's strategic shift is to make AI Cabinet the governance and orchestration core, while the public site becomes an intelligence hub rather than a content feed.
systemic_effects: Content production becomes a controlled pipeline rather than isolated drafting.
Editorial trust depends on source visibility, confidence, and approval states.
Distribution becomes a governed transformation layer, not a direct AI action.
next_orientation_step: Implement Orientation Object schemas and use them as the source-of-truth layer before building channel-specific publishing tools.
